deliverables: Periodic independent audits of treasury fund use and oversight metrics
Eternl Core rewrite, Eternl Hub, enhanced hardware wallet support, and wallet data export improvements
request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund 12 months of Eternl operations, maintenance, and improvements from August 2026 to July 2027.

claims.claim: Eternl is a non-custodial Cardano light wallet available on web, browser extension, Android, and iOS.
The proposal requests ₳2,350,000, valued at about $0.1787 per Ada, to cover an annual operating cost of about $420,000.
The budget allocates 55% to frontend, 25% to backend, 5% to support, 13% to admin, and 2% to audits.
The proposal funds 6.0 FTE distributed across 10 contributors at $70,000 per FTE.
Eternl has about 100,000 browser extension installs and about 30,000 Android and iOS installs.
If roughly 5,500 users, or about 4.2% of the install base, buy the Pro plan, Pro income would fully cover the annual $420,000 cost.
The proposer states that 10-18% of Cardano mainnet transactions are conducted via Eternl.

The proposer commits to converting up to $420,000 worth of Ada into stablecoins, returning any Ada above that amount to the treasury, and holding funds in an auditable account that abstains from voting and is not delegated to an SPO.
Independent audits of treasury fund use are planned for February 2027 and August 2027 by a party unaffiliated with Tastenkunst GmbH or the Eternl team.
The main Eternl UI will not be open-source, though some libraries used in Eternl will be published through the npm registry.

summary: The document describes a ₳2,350,000 non-milestone treasury request administered by Tastenkunst GmbH to sustain Eternl for 12 months, with budget details, repayment mechanics, audit plans, claimed adoption, and a Pro-plan path toward sustainability.
